title: Inhabitation reduces to a scalar root equation per law
statement: For d_psi = d_lambda = 1 and any partition q at tilt beta, sum_b W_b t_b mu_lambda_b = I_psilambda(q) - beta I_lambdalambda(q), with t_b = mu_psi_b - beta mu_lambda_b. When I_lambdalambda(q) > 0, division gives B*(I_q) - beta; when it is zero, B*(I_q) is undefined although the numerator identity remains valid. For positive-mass atomless strip rules the numerator is E[h(T_beta) S_lambda], and regular self-consistency decomposes into Lloyd stationarity plus this root equation. NECESSITY ONLY: for any atomless law with (M4), full-triple empirical inhabitation at fixed (kappa,c_0,gamma) requires a population root with |beta| <= 2M/kappa, lambda_min(I_q) >= kappa, masses >= c_0, and t-mean separation >= gamma. No converse or empirical basin-transfer theorem is claimed. Finite root searches are measured probes, not decisions or uniqueness proofs.
assumptions: d_psi = d_lambda = 1; the numerator identity is exact for every law and partition; the quotient and B*(I_q) require I_lambdalambda(q) > 0
the strip/step-function form needs positive cell masses; atomlessness makes ordered interval means strictly increasing and tie boundaries null

necessity imports DS14 (audited) via the pathwise DS17.0 lemma; sufficiency (root => inhabited empirical sequences) is NOT claimed - the empirical transfer off class (L) is open and recorded in OP29(a)/OP30 rescope
the compact tilt bound |beta| <= 2M/kappa is the audited DS14 parameter-class bound

proof_location.section: DS17. Inhabitation of the margin-certified branch: the conditional-centering obstruction and the fixed-point gate

role: a necessary per-law population test for inhabitation: one scalar root equation over all Lloyd-stationary branches
warning: Audit-hardened. A root is necessary, not sufficient: nothing proves finite exchange-stable sequences reach a root's basin. The compact beta window depends on the declared kappa; a hard-coded [-2.5,2.5] scan is not the theorem's full range. Dense or branch-tracked numerical searches cannot certify absence or uniqueness without a separate root-count proof.
